# Enable API gateway for Kubernetes

Before Consul 2.0, the API group `gateway.networking.k8s.io` managed API gateways, called Standard API gateway. Consul 2.0 introduces the Consul API gateway controller and the new API gateway CRDs under the API Group `consul.hashicorp.com`.
We recommend the standard API gateway installation approach, which is the default installation choice. It uses the API Group `gateway.networking.k8s.io`.
Use the Consul API gateway controller for the platforms that manage gateway CRDs under the API group `gateway.networking.k8s.io` in version `v1` and is below 1.6.0 package version of the API group `gateway.networking.k8s.io`.

Both controllers are supported by Consul's Helm chart.

Before you begin the installation process, verify that the environment you are deploying Consul and the API gateway in meets the requirements listed in the [Technical Specifications](/consul/docs/north-south/api-gateway/k8s/tech-specs). Refer to the [Release Notes](/consul/docs/release-notes) for any additional information about the version you are deploying.

If the platform manages the gateway CRDs under the API group `gateway.networking.k8s.io` or if any other application or user externally installed these CRDs, set `global.installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false`.

1. The Consul Helm chart deploys the Standard/Consul API gateway using the configuration specified in the `values.yaml` file. Refer to [Helm Chart Configuration - `connectInject.apiGateway`](/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#apigateway) for information about the Helm chart configuration options. Create a `values.yaml` file for configuring your Consul API gateway deployment and include the following settings:

  <Tabs>

    <Tab heading="Reference configuration to deploy Standard API gateway only">
    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      crds:
        enableTcpRoute: true
        consulapi:
          enabled: false
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="Reference configuration to deploy Consul API gateway">
    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      crds:
        consulapi:
          enabled: true
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
    ```

    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OpenShift (OCP <=4.18) for Standard API gateway">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: true
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: true
          consulapi:
            enabled: false
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
      cni:
        enabled: true
        logLevel: info
        multus: true
        cniBinDir: "/var/lib/cni/bin"
        cniNetDir: "/etc/kubernetes/cni/net.d"
     ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="OpenShift (OCP >=4.19) for Standard API gateway without TCP route CRD">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
          consulapi:
            enabled: false
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
      cni:
        enabled: true
        logLevel: info
        multus: true
        cniBinDir: "/var/lib/cni/bin"
        cniNetDir: "/etc/kubernetes/cni/net.d"
    ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

     <Tab heading="OpenShift (OCP >=4.19) for Consul API gateway to support TCP route CRD">

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      openshift:
        enabled: true
        crds:
          enableTcpRoute: false
          consulapi:
            enabled: true
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: true
      cni:
        enabled: true
        logLevel: info
        multus: true
        cniBinDir: "/var/lib/cni/bin"
        cniNetDir: "/etc/kubernetes/cni/net.d"
    ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="GKE Autopilot">

    By default, GKE Autopilot installs [Gateway API resources](https://gateway-api.sigs.k8s.io).

    The following working example enables both Consul Service Mesh and Standard API gateway on GKE Autopilot. Refer to [`connectInject.agiGateway` in the Helm chart reference](https://developer.hashicorp.com/consul/docs/reference/k8s/helm#v-connectinject-apigateway) for additional information.
    To support TCP route CRDs use Consul API gateway by setting `global.crds.consulapi.enabled: true`.

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      crds:
        consulapi:
          enabled: false
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: false
        manageNonStandardCRDs: true
     ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>

    <Tab heading="Kubernetes Clusters with Gateway CRDs managed by cluster platforms">

    To support TCP route CRDs use Consul API gateway by setting `global.crds.consulapi.enabled: true`.

    <CodeBlockConfig filename="values.yaml">

    ```yaml
    global:
      installK8sNetworkingCRDs: false
      crds:
        consulapi:
          enabled: false
    connectInject:
      enabled: true
      apiGateway:
        manageExternalCRDs: false
        manageNonStandardCRDs: true
     ```
    </CodeBlockConfig>
    </Tab>
  </Tabs>


## API gateway Reconciliation

Consul only reconciles API gateway resources that meet specific requirements. For Consul to manage an API gateway, the gateway must:

1. Include the required labels in the gateway metadata

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="Standard API gateway">

<CodeBlockConfig>

```yaml
labels:
  component: api-gateway  
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Consul API gateway">

<CodeBlockConfig>

```yaml
labels:
  component: api-gateway-consul 
```

</CodeBlockConfig>
</Tab>

</Tabs>
2. Specify the correct controller name that matches the gateway type.

Consul validates both criterias before reconciling the gateway object.

## Standard API gateway

For the standard Kubernetes Gateway API that uses API Group `gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1`, the gateway must:
- Set the `gatewayClassName` to reference a GatewayClass with controller name `consul.hashicorp.com/gateway-controller`
- Include the label `component: api-gateway` in the metadata

Example configuration:

<CodeBlockConfig>

```yaml
apiVersion: gateway.networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: api-gateway # can be modified 
  namespace: consul # can be modified
  labels:
    component: api-gateway # Do not modify this
```

</CodeBlockConfig>

## Consul API gateway

For the  Consul Gateway resource (using API Group `consul.hashicorp.com/v1beta1`), the gateway must:
- Set the `gatewayClassName` to reference a GatewayClass with controller name `consul.hashicorp.com/gateway-controller-consul`
- Include the label `component: api-gateway-consul` in the metadata

Example configuration:

<CodeBlockConfig>

```yaml
apiVersion: consul.hashicorp.com/v1beta1
kind: Gateway
metadata:
  name: api-gateway-consul # can be modified
  namespace: consul # can be modified
  labels:
    component: api-gateway-consul # Do not modify this
```

</CodeBlockConfig>
